project.name: Septikon Online
project.purpose: Online implementation of the Septikon board game for two players.

team_work_split.integration_rule: Backend is the source of truth for game state and rules. Frontend renders server state and sends player actions.

transport.realtime: WebSocket is not yet confirmed as implemented; use HTTP polling for the initial frontend.

verification.latest_reported_result: All packages passed or compiled successfully in the latest reported run.
verification.important_note: Run the command again against the current checkout before integration; this file is a handoff snapshot, not a live inspection of the repository.

game_rules_and_constraints.board_requirement: The board layout and compartment arrangement must match the board image and official rules supplied by the user. Do not invent a simplified or alternative board.
game_rules_and_constraints.turn_flow: A turn includes a dice roll and a main action, subject to the backend's current validation.
game_rules_and_constraints.robots: Robot movement is tied to the dice roll and server-side game rules.
game_rules_and_constraints.rockets: Rocket progression is handled by game logic over turns.
game_rules_and_constraints.production_and_repairs: Production and repair are time/turn-based game processes handled by the backend.
game_rules_and_constraints.starting_resources_note: Confirm against the current backend initialization before displaying these as immutable UI constants.

known_api_routes_from_prior_handoff.purpose: Get room and current game state
Start or perform a repair action

api_contract_caveats: The route list is reconstructed from previous project discussions and must be checked against the current router before frontend integration.
Exact request body fields, response envelopes, error formats, and JSON property casing must be copied from the current Go handlers and structs.
A previous handoff mentioned playerID in action request bodies; verify exact casing and required fields in the current code.
Do not assume that add-robot, production, resource collection, rocket launch/control, or repair-status routes are available until verified.
known_gaps_or_follow_up: Verify every route and its exact request/response schema against current handlers.
Complete any missing action endpoints needed by the full rules: robot creation, production, resource collection, rocket actions, and task/status retrieval as applicable.
Add or verify validation for robot movement paths and action connectivity.
Review concurrent room/game state updates and disconnect handling.
Authentication/player identity strategy is not confirmed as complete.
Persistent storage is not confirmed; current state has previously been described as in-memory.
WebSocket/realtime updates are not confirmed; HTTP polling is the initial integration approach.
Victory/end-condition handling should be verified against the full rules.

proposed_stack.styling: CSS Modules or plain CSS initially
proposed_stack.status: Proposal only; confirm with the frontend developer before scaffolding.

core_principles: Backend is authoritative for all game rules and state.
Do not duplicate dice, movement, production, repair, rocket, resource, or victory calculations in the browser.
After an action, refresh the room/game state from the backend.
Identify the local player using the player ID returned or assigned by the backend; do not infer identity from array order.
Show loading, validation, network, and server-error states.
Disable actions that the server reports as unavailable; still handle server-side rejection gracefully.
Initially poll GET /api/rooms/{id} approximately every 1-2 seconds while a game is active, then replace or supplement polling when WebSocket support exists.
suggested_ui_areas: Board view matching the supplied board image and rules
suggested_initial_milestones: Create React + TypeScript + Vite application and environment configuration.
Implement API client and typed interfaces from verified backend JSON.
Implement health check and room list/create/join flows.
Implement waiting room and player identity handling.
Render board from backend board data without hardcoding game state.
Implement turn display, dice roll, and end-turn flow.
Add robot, repair, production, resource, and rocket UI as their endpoints are verified.
Test two browser sessions against the same backend room.

handoff_checklist: Open the current backend repository and run go test ./...
Check the actual HTTP router and record all registered routes.
Check Go JSON tags and copy exact request/response schemas into frontend-contract.md.
Confirm CORS settings for the frontend development origin.
Confirm whether player IDs are generated by the backend or supplied by the client.
Confirm whether room state is in-memory and what happens after server restart.
Agree on React + TypeScript + Vite or replace the proposed stack.
Start frontend with room flow and read-only game-state rendering before implementing every action.
